answer: In the agent grove, each identity must lock a portion of stake into a time-bound vault that releases only after sustained attestation activity. The vault carries an umber penalty fee if withdrawn early, and the outer layer is a velvet bond that multiplies the required lock for new identities. An attacker creating sybils must fund many such locks simultaneously, paying real capital costs that cannot be recycled quickly, while honest participants accumulate deeper positions at lower relative expense.
